title: prefill-decode: chunked speculative prefill + stage overlap + kernel scheduler + KV cache improvements
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: reduce end-to-end latency and GPU memory pressure for long-prefill workloads by increasing overlap between prefill and decode stages, making prefill chunked and speculative, and stabilizing kernel scheduling and KV cache access paths. This PR combines several complementary optimizations: 1) chunked prefill: break long prefill sequences into smaller chunks to enable streaming KV population and earlier decode start; 2) speculative prefill: start speculative decode work on partial KV state when model/backpressure heuristics indicate a high-confidence path; 3) stage overlap: extend and formalize prefill->decode overlap windows and backpressure signals between stages; 4) kernel scheduler heuristics: reduce kernel-switching thrash by batching like-kernel invocations and preferring fast paths for quantized kernels; 5) KV cache improvements: shard KV cache across worker lanes and add a lock-free read path to reduce contention during aggressive batching. Results: microbench harness (bert-like 2k prefill + 512 decode) shows median latency down ~12% and p99 down ~18% for mixed workloads; throughput improves ~18% for 8-concurrent-stream scenarios; GPU memory for prefill buffers reduced ~22% due to chunking and early eviction of stale KV frames. Backwards compatibility: changes are opt-in via runtime config flags (prefill.chunk_size, prefill.speculative.enabled, scheduler.mode, kv.shard_count). Default rollout sets conservative chunk sizes and speculative thresholds. Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked (linear: ENG-2245) and perf benchmarks added
- [x] Unit tests for new scheduler heuristics and KV sharding
- [x] Integration tests for streaming prefill+decode overlap
- [x] Canary rollout plan in console and feature flags
- [x] Observability: added metrics for prefill-latency, speculative-hit-rate, kernel-switch-count
Test plan: run perf-canary jobs across instance types (a100, h100, triton-backed nodes) with existing benchmark-lab scenarios. Validate no regression on short-prefill workloads and ensure graceful fallback to non-speculative path on misprediction. Rollout: feature-flagged rollout staged by customer tier -> internal canary -> 10% hosted -> 50% -> 100% across regions. Related: also touches kernel selection and scheduling work in ENG-2367. Links: design doc (linear ENG-2245), benchmark results attached in commits, issue SUP-1178 for KV contention seen in production incident-2026-01. Notes: kept changes modular to ease reverts; merged with squash on main.
commits: Add chunked prefill pipeline and chunking utilities - split long prefill into configurable chunks - KV population streaming hooks
Introduce speculative prefill path and misprediction rollback - thresholding and confidence estimator - metrics for speculative-hit-rate
Kernel scheduler heuristics - group same-kernel batches - add fast-path preference for int8 kernels
KV cache sharding and lock-free read path - shard count config and per-lane eviction policy - lock-free reader with epoch-based consistency
Tests and benchmarks - unit tests, integration tests, perf harness updates, canary configs
review_comments: Ethan Cole: Left a few nits around config naming and suggested adding a conservative default for chunk_size. Also asked for a safety net to disable speculative prefill per-customer.
Ava Martinez: Addressed config naming and added per-customer disable flag. Added unit test for fallback path and updated docs.
Priya Nair: Requested additional telemetry for kernel-switch-count and a breakdown by kernel type. Found race in KV eviction under heavy load (fixed by epoch-based guard).
Liam Chen: Approved after fixes; noted that scheduler heuristic thresholds should be easy to tune from the console.
release_notes: Improved prefill-decode latency and throughput via chunked and speculative prefill, kernel scheduler heuristics, and KV cache sharding/lock-free reads. Opt-in via runtime flags; rollout will be staged. See ENG-2245 for design and perf details.
